title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 21
paragraphs: So these men perished in this way, both they themselves and their whole train of servants; for carriages and servants and all the usual pomp of equipage had come with them, and all of it was made away with at the same time as they were. Afterwards, not long after, the Persians made a great search for these men, and Alexander halted the search by a clever stroke: by giving large sums of money and his own sister, whose name was Gygaea—by giving these things, I say, to Bubares, a Persian in command of those searching for the murdered men, Alexander halted their search.
